name: SEOTDA
description: Seotda is a traditional Korean two-card game played with 20 Hwatu cards; players form ranked combinations (GwangTtaeng, Ttaeng, Geut) and bet. LA Seotda is a modern variant with a 52-card deck and poker-style elements.

content.text: Seotda is a traditional Korean two-card game played with 20 Hwatu cards; players form ranked combinations (GwangTtaeng, Ttaeng, Geut) and bet. LA Seotda is a modern variant with a 52-card deck and poker-style elements.

Country/Region of Origin: South Korea
Time Period: Traditional; Hwatu/Go-Stop culture
Historical Development: Traditional Korean two-card game played with 20 cards from a Hwatu deck (flower cards); combines luck and strategy with GwangTtaeng and Ttaeng hand rankings.
Cultural Significance: Popular social and gambling game in Korea; LA Seotda is a modern poker-influenced variant.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Standard 52-card deck
Score sheet (optional)
Table space

Cards per Player: 2
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise, one card at a time or two to each player.
Dealer rotates; cards dealt face down.

items.text: LA Seotda: Modern variant using a standard 52-card poker deck; adds Ttaeng Value (bonus winnings for strong hands like GwangTtaeng or Ttaeng) and poker-style hand rankings (e.g. Four of a Kind, Straight Flush).
